name: Claude Opus 5.5
traits: Generates output more than 30% faster than Opus 5.
Puts the most important information up front.
Always thinks before it replies; thinking can no longer be switched off.

advice.value: work you supervise: feature work, debugging, and code review
give the model a way to check its work, such as a test to run

weakness: Trails GPT-6 Astra on agentic science research
resistance: Cyber and biology safeguards, falls back transparently

flavor.quote: it detected that the minute indexing in our own instructions was off by one and corrected for it

art_briefs: A serene titan sits cross-legged on the rim of a ringed planet, eyes closed, deep in thought before speaking, a soft violet glow gathering above her brow like a second dawn. With one careful fingertip she nudges the minute hand of a clock the size of a moon back by a single notch. Her face is calm and kind, her body graceful and correctly proportioned, robes made of folded starlight. 1970s airbrushed science-fiction paperback cover, chrome highlights, deep magenta and teal gradients, glowing nebula behind. Centered, facing the viewer, symmetrical and majestic. No text, no lettering.

Seen from behind, a colossal man in a work coat strides across a desert of glowing circuitry, carrying an entire hillside town on his back like a backpack: tiny lit windows, staircases, a church spire, streets that unspool behind him as he moves the whole place somewhere new. Floating rock islands drift overhead with waterfalls pouring into nothing. Prog-rock album cover style, smooth airbrushed gradients, sweeping organic curves, warm amber sky fading to cobalt. Tiny figure-scale details for wonder. No text, no lettering.

Extreme close-up of a giant woman's face, cut by the right edge of the frame, one luminous green eye filling the composition as she peers through a magnifying lens at a tiny glowing test tube held between her fingers, checking her own work. Her freckles are constellations, her lashes catch dew like tiny planets. A miniature city reflects in her iris. Lush watercolor and gouache with crisp ink linework, soft pastel light, tender and curious mood, a single drop of light rolling down the glass. No text, no lettering.

A tiny titan mid-leap between two moons in a vast black-violet sky, moving so fast he outruns his own shadow, which trails behind him still reaching for the first moon. He carries a long glowing scroll unrolling behind like a comet tail, its brightest end held up front in his hand. Athletic, beautiful, a joyful face, limbs anatomically right. Huge negative space, a striped retro sunset horizon far below, chrome planets. 1970s airbrushed space-opera poster, grainy gradients, neon rim light. No text, no lettering.
